title: 02. Tool Calling & MCP: Tool Chaining
summary: Tool Chaining: explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     TOOL CHAINING                               │
│  "Output of one tool feeds as input to next tool"               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  EXAMPLE: "Find Python articles and analyze reading time"
  
  STEP 1: web_search("Python tutorials 2024")
  Output: [
    {"title": "Python Tips", "url": "...", "snippet": "..."},
    {"title": "Python Guide", "url": "...", "snippet": "..."},
  ]
                    │
                    ▼ (output becomes input)
  STEP 2: fetch_url(url="...python-tips-url...")
  Output: {"content": "Full article text... 2500 words..."}
                    │
                    ▼ (output becomes input)
  STEP 3: word_counter(text="Full article text...")
  Output: {"words": 2500, "reading_time_mins": 10}
                    │
                    ▼ (output becomes input)
  STEP 4: summarizer(text="Full article text...", max_points=5)
  Output: {"summary": "...", "key_points": [...]}
  
  FINAL ANSWER: "The article has 2500 words (~10 min read).
                 Key points: ..."
  
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  TYPES OF CHAINING:
  
  LINEAR:    A → B → C → D          (each feeds the next)
  
  BRANCHING: A → B → D              (B and C run from A,
               ↘ C → D               both feed D)
  
  PARALLEL:  A ──→ B ──┐            (B, C, D all start
             A ──→ C ──┤→ E          from A simultaneously)
             A ──→ D ──┘
  
  CONDITIONAL: A → B → if result>X: C else: D
```
